digest.component_or_area: structured-output orchestration seam (RP-01 Pydantic AI migration)
propositions: Historical Rebar structured-output behavior including deterministic repair, schema extraction, three-attempt ceiling, stop-reason fast-fail, derived budgets, fallback predicate/order, durable usage telemetry, and terminal typed failure taxonomy must be preserved or deliberately approved as intentional changes during Pydantic AI 1.107.2 migration.

Offline in-process integration probe exercised 32 real Pydantic AI seams (Agent, output modes, retry, UsageLimits, FallbackModel, Hooks, ProcessHistory) with mocked-only provider transport and confirmed that decisions around complete-response-on-fit, aggregate successful-run usage, cause-chain exception restoration, and trace-based candidate observability all satisfy historical constraints.

One operation-wide Pydantic request_limit shared by tool turns and output-validation retries is approved with a documented raise-the-limit follow-up plan; retry-wire policy sends complete failed response only when deterministic fit is proven, otherwise omits it whole; length/max_tokens rejection is bounded with concise-response guidance; refusal/content-filter remains terminal.

Exhaustion exception handling re-raises only exact Rebar-owned StructuredOutputError found in Pydantic cause chain; candidate-attempt observability uses public model instrumentation trace events rather than synthesized token usage; no token spend is fabricated for failed attempts without provider-reported usage.

All 15 historical ticket aliases and their behavioral cases were deduplicated against the Pydantic AI 1.107.2 native and prompted output modes, fallback predicates, usage limits, and failure-matrix tests; 290 passing tests across 13 source suites validate current Rebar behavior and 407 total focused tests across two runs confirm regression coverage.

Four phases of approval are recorded: (1) one-wide request budget + raise-limit caveat; (2) complete response on proven fit, omit whole if unfit; (3) aggregate successful-run usage; (4) cause-chain-exact exception restoration and trace-based candidate observability; all decisions preserve historical authority and no maintainer approval remains pending for RP-01 implementation ticketization.
